title: Kinetic Press canonical animation construction roadmap v9
summary: Preserve the architecture-pressure roadmap, mark quadratic branching complete, and make canonical animation construction the sole current implementation phase.

sourceRefs.summary: User-approved exact 30-slice construction and governed round-trip program.
Approved predecessor retaining the complete architecture-pressure roadmap.

progress.summary: Quadratic branching and its bounded presentation-governance follow-up are resolved. The approved canonical animation construction contract is executing as the sole current implementation authority.

planRevision.objective: Grow Kinetic Press through reusable semantic and visual primitives: preserve accepted exemplars, prove canonical animation construction and governed round trips now, then expand through calculus, linear algebra, arithmetic, precalculus, geometry/data, and cross-domain explanations in architecture-amortizing order.

assumptions.statement: The active approved Theseus plan is the only product-roadmap authority; the Workbench and summaries derive from it and do not own parallel lifecycle state.
An approved typed run contract, not a planned roadmap row, authorizes implementation and owns live slice status and verification.
Near-term exemplars are ordered by the reusable semantic, scheduling, rendering, and multi-view pressure they apply rather than by textbook chapter order.
Subjective motion and interaction work perfects one independently reversible exemplar and stops for human review before family-wide promotion.
Animated mathematical fragments may move independently, but exact native KaTeX owns the settled expression and its typography and spacing.
Semantic objects own mathematical identity, lineage, laws, and intent; renderers own geometry, timing, typography, routes, and accessibility.
Later and someday rows retain robust product coverage but do not authorize implementation until a reviewed run contract links to them.

phases.title: Gold equation reader
phases.objective: Maintain the accepted balanced-equation reader as the reference for measured motion, native settlement, responsive layout, and exact seek and rewind.
phases.architectureBenefit: Canonical measured-motion and native-settlement reference.
phases.rationale: Every later symbolic animation needs one stable presentation benchmark.

phases.title: Distribution and factoring grammar
phases.objective: Represent fan-out distribution, collection, factoring, ordering, and reversible choreography through shared semantic roles and laws.
phases.architectureBenefit: Shared one-to-many lineage and reversible scheduling.
phases.rationale: Distribution was the first pressure test beyond one-to-one token motion.

phases.title: Fraction composition architecture
phases.objective: Carry opaque fractions through distribution, normalization, composition, reverse factoring, and a complete solve trace without renderer-owned algebra.
phases.architectureBenefit: Opaque subtree identity and schedule-independent composition.
phases.rationale: It proves structured algebra can compose without flattening fractions into glyph tricks.

phases.title: Generated symbolic transform library
phases.objective: Compile governed symbolic requests into verified semantic animation fixtures while keeping providers outside math text, timing, geometry, and rendering authority.
phases.architectureBenefit: Reusable verified-operation pipeline with bounded LLM authority.
phases.rationale: Generation becomes safe only after the semantic and rendering ownership boundary is enforceable.

phases.title: Derivative secant-to-tangent
phases.objective: Synchronize a finite difference quotient, moving graph point, secant slope, and tangent limit from one shared parameter.
phases.architectureBenefit: Shared-clock multi-representation convergence.
phases.rationale: It is the smallest strong pressure test for symbolic, graph, and limit continuity.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Secant to tangent for f(x) = x^3

phases.title: Governed semantic authoring
phases.objective: Accept provider-shaped semantic intent only after exact operation, role, law, lifecycle, pacing, provenance, and normal-form verification.
phases.architectureBenefit: Provider-independent compiler and authority firewall.
phases.rationale: The authoring boundary must be proven before subject breadth multiplies generated assets.

phases.title: Semantic Animation Workbench
phases.objective: Provide one searchable editor surface for canonical animations, real representations, acceptance evidence, lifecycle state, and item-scoped review.
phases.architectureBenefit: Unified inspection control plane over existing authorities.
phases.rationale: A single exploration surface became necessary once exemplar and representation counts grew.

phases.title: Authoritative roadmap Workbench
phases.objective: Project the active approved plan into a simple sortable Workbench table while preserving one roadmap authority and stable incremental interaction.
phases.architectureBenefit: Discoverable roadmap without replicated lifecycle state.
phases.rationale: Product progress and future coverage must remain legible before more animation families are added.

phases.title: Exact radical native settlement
phases.objective: Eliminate reverse-playback flicker by recomposing independently moving exponent fragments into one measured source block and handing off to the exact native radical endpoint.
phases.architectureBenefit: Composite fragment motion with exact typographic endpoint ownership.
phases.rationale: The remaining radical defect isolates a reusable native-settlement problem before broader fractional powers.

phases.title: Semantic animation convergence
phases.objective: Converge the semantic-animation compiler into one enforceable dependency direction, typed presentation seam, canonical sampled-frame convention, narrow asset projections, and classified compatibility surface while preserving the accepted gold cohort.
phases.architectureBenefit: One-way compiler ownership, typed presentation policy, shared frame laws, and bounded compatibility debt.
phases.rationale: The maintained lesson cohort now supplies preservation evidence, while continued domain expansion would multiply ambiguous compiler stages and compatibility paths.

phases.title: Quadratic semantic branching
phases.objective: Model completing the square and quadratic-formula paths as explicit lawful branches that converge on verified roots.
phases.architectureBenefit: Branch scheduling, convergence, and alternative solution-path semantics.
phases.rationale: The semantic branching and bounded presentation-governance contracts are resolved; the retained exemplar remains evidence rather than current implementation authority.

phases.title: Canonical animation construction
phases.objective: Prove one semantic-to-renderer construction path, migrate one fraction split/merge reader transition exclusively, and establish governed variation plus browser-native review without parallel runtimes.
phases.architectureBenefit: One composable human and governed-model construction path with compiler-owned mathematics, presentation, rendering, and repair.
phases.rationale: Renderer convergence closed the implementation fork; construction is now the narrowest bottleneck to visible library growth without parallel animation systems.

phases.title: Integral accumulation
phases.objective: Synchronize partition refinement, region accumulation, symbolic sums, and the limiting integral.
phases.architectureBenefit: Many-object refinement and accumulation under one semantic clock.
phases.rationale: It follows branching because it adds large synchronized collections and limit continuity.

phases.title: Vector and dot-product projection
phases.objective: Coordinate vector components, geometric projection, magnitude, angle, and dot-product notation.
phases.architectureBenefit: Coordinate-to-geometry identity across multiple views.
phases.rationale: It pressure-tests persistent identity between symbolic components and spatial objects.

phases.title: Matrix-vector linear map
phases.objective: Show matrix entries, row computations, basis movement, and geometric transformation as one linear map.
phases.architectureBenefit: Grid structure, nested composition, and spatial transformation.
phases.rationale: It compounds vector identity with structured table semantics and coordinated geometry.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Apply a 2 by 2 matrix to a vector

phases.title: Exact fractions and quantity models
phases.objective: Synchronize exact KaTeX fractions with partitioned circles, bars or areas, and number-line positions through shared quantity identity.
phases.architectureBenefit: One quantity model projected into symbolic and concrete representations.
phases.rationale: Fractions are the first arithmetic cohort because they stress synchronized multi-view identity rather than only digit motion.

phases.title: Multi-digit addition
phases.objective: Coordinate column addition, place-value exchange, regrouping marks, and a base-ten or area representation.
phases.architectureBenefit: Persistent place-value identity and carry scheduling.
phases.rationale: Addition establishes the reusable place-exchange primitive before harder written algorithms.

phases.title: Multi-digit subtraction
phases.objective: Coordinate decomposition across place values, borrowing notation, and quantity removal without losing digit identity.
phases.architectureBenefit: Reverse place exchange and dependency-aware scheduling.
phases.rationale: Subtraction reuses addition's place model while adding reverse exchange and zero-crossing dependencies.

phases.title: Multi-digit multiplication
phases.objective: Synchronize partial products, place shifts, the written algorithm, and an area decomposition.
phases.architectureBenefit: Two-dimensional decomposition and partial-result composition.
phases.rationale: Multiplication extends distribution and place-value primitives into a concrete arithmetic algorithm.

phases.title: Multi-digit division
phases.objective: Coordinate grouping, partial quotients, repeated subtraction, place descent, and remainder semantics.
phases.architectureBenefit: Iterative state, nested steps, and quotient-remainder invariants.
phases.rationale: Division is sequenced after the other operations because it composes their primitives into a longer dependency chain.

phases.title: Ratios, rates, percent, and units
phases.objective: Preserve quantity and unit identity through ratio tables, double number lines, percent scaling, and unit conversion.
phases.architectureBenefit: Unit-aware scaling across linked representations.
phases.rationale: This closes the arithmetic cohort by turning exact operations into applied proportional structure.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Scale a recipe and convert to percent

phases.title: Rational expressions
phases.objective: Animate common denominators, restrictions, cancellation, complex fractions, and rational equation solving with exact subtree identity.
phases.architectureBenefit: Domain constraints plus fraction composition at algebraic scale.
phases.rationale: It is the first post-arithmetic reuse of the opaque-fraction and cancellation architecture.

phases.title: Polynomial algebra
phases.objective: Cover collection, multiplication, factoring, long or synthetic division, remainder identity, and root-factor correspondence.
phases.architectureBenefit: Large symbolic schedules and reversible decomposition.
phases.rationale: Polynomial breadth amortizes distribution and quadratic branching before introducing new function families.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Factor and divide a cubic polynomial

phases.title: Exponent and logarithm laws
phases.objective: Cover product, quotient, power, zero, negative, and inverse log laws with fluent identity omissions such as x^1 and exact explanatory traces.
phases.architectureBenefit: Nested operator rewrites, fluent projections, and inverse-function continuity.
phases.rationale: This generalizes the approved exponent motifs only after the radical endpoint contract is exact.

phases.title: Fractional-power and radical generalization
phases.objective: Generalize fractional powers to higher radical indices, persistent numerator powers, reverse playback, and negative exponents that become reciprocal radical expressions.
phases.architectureBenefit: Parameterized composite morphs with persistent index and radicand structure.
phases.rationale: The explicitly recorded negative-exponent case belongs after the square-root exemplar proves exact composite settlement.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Rewrite x^(-2/3) as a reciprocal cube-root expression

phases.title: Functions and coordinate algebra
phases.objective: Coordinate evaluation, composition, inverse functions, graph transforms, domain and range, intercepts, and piecewise structure.
phases.architectureBenefit: Symbolic-to-graph identity and parameterized transform families.
phases.rationale: Function choreography reuses the derivative multi-view clock at broader curricular scale.

phases.title: Equations, inequalities, and systems
phases.objective: Cover equivalence-preserving solves, interval branches, sign reversals, substitution, elimination, and intersections.
phases.architectureBenefit: Constraint sets, branching intervals, and multi-equation identity.
phases.rationale: This broadens the gold reader only after shared branch semantics exist.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Solve a two-variable system by elimination

phases.title: Trigonometry
phases.objective: Synchronize unit-circle motion, triangle ratios, graphs, identities, inverse branches, and periodic wrapping.
phases.architectureBenefit: Periodic clocks and three-way geometric-symbolic-graph identity.
phases.rationale: Trigonometry benefits from the mature multi-view and branch machinery built by calculus and functions.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Trace sine across the unit circle and graph

phases.title: Sequences and large operators
phases.objective: Animate indexed sequences, recurrence, finite and infinite series, sigma and product notation, and convergence.
phases.architectureBenefit: Indexed traversal, folding, and large-operator structure.
phases.rationale: Sequences reuse accumulation while introducing discrete index ownership and recurrence.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Build a geometric series from partial sums

phases.title: Euclidean geometry
phases.objective: Cover construction, congruence, similarity, the Pythagorean theorem, area, surface area, and volume with diagram-linked proof steps.
phases.architectureBenefit: Diagram topology, proof correspondence, and spatial decomposition.
phases.rationale: Geometry starts after core symbolic multi-view contracts because diagrams add a distinct spatial authoring surface.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Rearrangement proof of the Pythagorean theorem

phases.title: Measurement, units, and scale
phases.objective: Link dimensions, conversions, scale drawings, coordinate geometry, and error or precision to visible quantities.
phases.architectureBenefit: Typed units, dimensional invariants, and scale-preserving transforms.
phases.rationale: Measurement extends the proportional-reasoning unit model into spatial contexts.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Convert and scale a floor plan

phases.title: Probability
phases.objective: Cover sample spaces, tree diagrams, combinatorics, conditional probability, independence, and expected value.
phases.architectureBenefit: Weighted branching, path aggregation, and conditional state.
phases.rationale: Probability reuses branch semantics while adding weights and aggregated outcomes.

phases.title: Data and statistics
phases.objective: Coordinate tables, distributions, center, spread, sampling, uncertainty, and data-to-graph transformations.
phases.architectureBenefit: Dataset identity across tables, plots, summaries, and uncertainty views.
phases.rationale: Data work follows probability because it requires stable collection identity and uncertainty semantics.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Transform a dataset into linked plots and summaries

phases.title: Programming and algorithms
phases.objective: Synchronize code execution, variable state, data structures, and graph traversal for BFS and Dijkstra-style explanations.
phases.architectureBenefit: Trace semantics and synchronized code-state-diagram views.
phases.rationale: Programming is the first cross-domain pressure test because its execution state is explicit and verifiable.
phases.canonicalExemplar: BFS traversal across code, queue, and graph

phases.title: Economics and parametric models
phases.objective: Link equations, curves, parameter changes, intersections, and narrative interpretation in supply-demand models.
phases.architectureBenefit: Parameterized graph systems and narrative-to-model correspondence.
phases.rationale: Economics reuses graph and intersection semantics with domain-specific explanatory prose.

phases.title: Physics work and energy
phases.objective: Synchronize force, displacement, energy equations, graphs, and diagrams through a conserved physical model.
phases.architectureBenefit: Quantity conservation across symbolic, graph, and spatial representations.
phases.rationale: Physics combines unit-aware arithmetic, calculus, diagrams, and conservation after those primitives mature.
phases.canonicalExemplar: Work-energy theorem across force and motion

phases.title: Cross-domain governed authoring
phases.objective: Extend the verified semantic-authoring boundary to domain adapters while preserving exact source provenance and renderer independence.
phases.architectureBenefit: Domain-extensible generation without provider-owned presentation.
phases.rationale: Cross-domain generation comes last so governance is tested against mature hand-authored references in each domain.

approval.rationale: Reconcile the resolved quadratic phase and select the user-approved canonical animation construction contract as the sole current implementation phase.
